text:
incidents-bot: Paging on-call — SEV2: text-generation API error rate >15% for model redwood-0. Paged @morgan and @alex. See https://redwood.internal/incidents/1758801234 :rotating_light:

morgan: ack, I'm on it. hitting the dashboard now. any obvious config rollouts?

alex: I'm stepping in if needed. quick Q: is this across regions or a single region?

morgan: looks like US-west primarily, but there's elevated errors in us-east too (smaller).

jit: I grabbed logs from the proxy layer — lots of 502s with `upstream reset` from runtime-2.

morgan: ok. @jit paste a short tail of the error stream here?

jit: here, latest 20 lines:
```
2025-11-06T02:10:12Z runtime-2 ERROR request_id=abcd123 conn=1001 upstream reset
2025-11-06T02:10:14Z runtime-2 ERROR request_id=abce124 conn=1009 upstream reset
2025-11-06T02:10:15Z runtime-2 ERROR request_id=      conn=1010 upstream reset
```
Note: some request_id fields blank — odd.

emily: that blank request_id rings a bell — we had a sampling tweak last week. can someone check the log-collector config?

paul: I'm looking at the log-collector agent rollout. There's a canary from 2025-11-05 that changed sampling from 100% -> 10% when incoming TPS > 2k. It was supposed to be opt-in.

morgan: if sampling dropped to 10% for high TPS we're going to be missing traces which makes triage hard. that's an observability gap.

alex: but the customer impact is real: error rate spiking. metrics show token failures at the runtime layer not just missing logs. we need a mitigation path first.

morgan: mitigation: 1) scale up runtime-2 pool, 2) route traffic away from runtime-2 to runtime-3, 3) temporarily revert collector sampling. who's available to revert?

paul: I can revert the sampler in 2 minutes. rolling back the canary to previous agent image.

ops-bot: deploy started: log-collector/agent canary rollback by paul — https://deploys.internal/12345

morgan: alex, can you ramp a new route to runtime-3? add a 20% shift now and monitor.

alex: doing a 20% shift now via traffic-router. command: `trafficctl shift --from runtime-2 --to runtime-3 --percent 20`

alex: shift complete. monitoring latency and 5xxs.

morgan: timeline note (for RCA): root event time = 2025-11-06T02:09:50Z pager fired.

jit: after the shift 5xxs dropped ~30% but still elevated. I'm seeing `upstream reset` traces that look like OOMs inside runtime-2 at 02:08-02:12. Sharing heap hist snippet:
```
runtime-2 heap OOMs 02:08-02:12: peaks at 92% memory, gc thrash
```

emily: memory spike could be caused by an unexpected tokenization pattern from a customer workload — but we need full logs. are we still missing request_ids from the collector?

paul: rollback applied. sampling set back to 100% for prod. ops-bot: rollback finished.

ops-bot: rollback succeeded: log-collector agents back to v2.3.1.

morgan: can anyone run an ad-hoc query to rehydrate logs for 02:06-02:14 with request_id present? I want to reconstruct the timeline and map requests to runtimes.

alex: running quick query in logsql: `select request_id, runtime, error, mem_percent from logs where ts between '2025-11-06T02:06:00Z' and '2025-11-06T02:14:00Z' and error is not null limit 200`

alex: results summary: 178 unique request_ids with errors, 64% attributed to runtime-2, 28% runtime-3, rest misc. multiple entries show `chunked payload` followed by OOM traces.

morgan: good. can we get sample full request payloads for a couple of failing request_ids? paste masked payloads — remove PII.

alex: pasted two samples: `req=abcd123` truncated payload -> large prompt with embedded base64 images (customer A). `req=afe321` small prompt but streaming enabled.

jit: hypothesis: a combination of large prompt and a regression in kernel memory handling under certain attention patterns caused the OOMs. The missing IDs were making it hard to confirm mapping between proxy resets and runtime OOM traces.

emily: agree. hypothesis tracking:
- H1: log sampling change hid correlations (status: supported)
- H2: runtime memory regression due to kernel change in 2025-11-04 build (status: investigating)
- H3: traffic spike from customer A caused overload (status: supported by payload samples)

morgan: next steps for in-incident RCA: 1) collect full heap dumps for runtime-2, 2) reproduce large prompt locally against the 11/04 build, 3) review kernel/allocator changes in PRs. assign owners.

jit: I'll grab heap dumps and upload to /tmp/incidents/1758801234/heapdumps.

paul: I'll coordinate the collector revert verification and add a note to the observability backlog to remove hidden sampling rollouts.

emily: I'll run a local repro with the sample prompt (sanitized) and compare memory profiles between v11/03 and v11/04 runtime builds.

morgan: for customer communication: impact window 02:06-02:22 UTC, affected customers had increased 5xx and timeouts. we should prepare a post-incident note with a timeline and mitigation steps. I'll draft an initial message for CS.

alex: also noticed a broken dashboard: the `runtime-ooms` chart was querying `logs_sampled` index which is backfilled only after sampling revert — dashboard showed a false negative earlier. need a dashboard correction to point at `logs_all` or metric-based counter.

morgan: add to observability gaps list: (a) sampling toggles applied silently, (b) dashboards using sampled logs, (c) missing request_id on some proxy resets.

ops-bot: handoff reminder — @morgan will be on call for next 25 minutes, then handoff to @alex unless incident resolved.

morgan: ongoing: collecting heap dumps, monitoring post-shift error rate. will update in 10m. please add any logs or repros you find here. :thumbsup:

paul: added a short runbook item: `if sampling drops unexpectedly, block rollout and alert channel` — PR opened: https://git.internal/r/prod-observability/pull/789

alex: error rate down to 4% after routing and rollback. keeping watch.

morgan: thanks team. leaving this thread open for the RCA docs. once we have heap dumps and repro, we'll move to postmortem channel.

incidents-bot: Incident state changed to "stabilized" at 2025-11-06T02:32:00Z.

morgan: closing timeline note: start 2025-11-06T02:09:50Z, mitigation routing+collector rollback at 02:12-02:18Z, stabilized 02:32Z. we'll schedule a deep-dive tomorrow.
